newsitem.title: USA: Fed approves NationsBank merger proposal.
newsitem.headline: Fed approves NationsBank merger proposal.

text.p: The Federal Reserve on Monday gave its blessing for Southeastern banking power NationsBank Corp. to expand into the Midwest by merging with Boatmen's BancShares Inc.

The $9-billion deal will make Charlotte, N.C.-based NationsBank the fourth largest bank in the United States with total assets of about $233 billion that represents nearly 6 percent of all U.S. banking assets.
The proposal has caused controversy. Opponents claim the banks do not lend enough in poorer communities and that many people face loss of their jobs because of the merger.

Moments after the Fed's regulatory approval, a community activist group announced it would try to block the deal in court. Inner City Press/Community on the Move claimed the Fed ignored evidence of discrimination in lending practices by NationsBank.
The group said it would seek a temporary stay blocking the merger while a federal appeals court reviewed the case.
But NationsBank said the charges were not warranted.
"NationsBank has a very strong community investment record and a record of results," said Pam McQuitty, a bank spokeswoman in Charlotte.
The Fed approved the deal unanimously, ruling that after review it had decided the lending records of both companies "(were) consistent with approval of this proposal."
NationsBank already is the fifth largest U.S. bank with assets of about $192.3 billion. Boatmen's is the 24th largest U.S. bank with assets of $40.7 billion.
NationsBank Chairman Hugh McColl has said previously there will be some layoffs. NationsBank has 67,000 employees and Boatmen's has 17,000.

In a 45-page decision, the Fed said it concluded "consummation of the proposal would not have a significantly adverse impact on competition or the concentration of banking resources in any relevant banking market."
The Fed noted that 15 groups had criticised the lending performance of NationsBank and Boatmen's in lower-income communities.

Recently, about 100 protestors including minority contractors picketed outside the New York Stock Exchange opposing the merger, saying they wanted NationsBank to adopt commitments to minority businesses as a condition of approval.

The Fed said its examiners had reviewed both banks' lending records, governed by the Community Reinvestment Act that commits banks not to discriminate in lending, and cited steps NationsBank has taken to boost lending to minority borrowers.
The proposed merger of NationsBank and Boatmen's was initially made public Aug. 30. They are seeking to complete the transaction in January.
Inner City Press/Community on the Move has claimed NationsBank's consumer finance unit charged "predatory" interest rates up to 20 percent "disproportionately to people of colour."
A spokeswoman for NationsBank has denied the charge, claiming the bank has a strong lending record and a diverse customer base that includes all races, genders and income levels.
